velocity_note: RECONCILED BEFORE QUOTING, per the PLAT-10 gate. As-scoped from docs/sprints/sprint-03.json: 26 items, 115 points. Computed by the tracker: planned 115, completed 107, parked 8, moved out 0, unfinished 0. The three figures agree, and moved-out is reported even though it is zero because a column that appears only when non-zero is a column nobody knows to look for. This is the first sprint where the moved-out ledger existed at all — PLAT-10 shipped it mid-sprint, and running `sprint velocity 2` afterwards re-stated Sprint 02 honestly for the first time: planned 77 (not the flattering 72), completed 72, moved out 5, unfinished 5. Sprint 02's recorded 100% is now visibly a description of nothing.
sizing_accuracy: Sizing held. Nothing was narrowed, nothing ran materially over its estimate, and no item left the sprint. The sprint GREW once, deliberately and mid-flight: it was planned at 52 points across 13 items on 27 Aug, and the owner added the premium redesign and the design system on 28 Aug, taking it to 115 across 26. That growth is recorded in the as-scoped file and is why planned reads 115 rather than 52 — it is information the next estimate needs, not drift. The one item that did not deliver, SEO-04, was not mis-sized: its gate fired, which is what the gate was for. DES-08 at 8 points was the largest single build and it was correctly the largest; DES-02 at 8 for three art directions was right; CONT-12 at 12 was sized on the larger shape before CONT-10 decided the count, and CONT-10 then decided DO-NOT-MERGE, which made 12 generous. That is the correct direction to be wrong in.

learnings.finding: PROSE RULES DO NOT FIRE. GATES AND SCRIPTS DO. This is the sprint's central finding and it governs how every future lesson is written. What fired: SEO-04's sourcing gate (twice, built nothing, correctly); DES-09's runnable check-guardrails.py; a writer's UNDO-before-write, because it was a DoD clause. What did not fire: 'resolve the operator before you rank a competitor' (persona prose, from Sprint 02's retro); 'ical re-arm the watcher' (skill prose); 'check the artefact the consumer receives' (doctrine prose). Sprint 02's retrospective had ALREADY recorded that five correct, committed, deployed rules failed to fire — and that finding was itself written in prose, and it then happened again.
learnings.why: The discriminator is not importance, it is FORM. When a retro names a lesson, the question is now which form it can take — a DoD clause, a pre-flight checklist item, a script, a gate that stops work — and prose only when none of those is possible. A lesson that can only be prose is one you should expect to repeat.

learnings.finding: THE CEO'S OWN VERIFICATION WAS WRONG NINE TIMES IN ONE SESSION, and every one is the same error: CHECKED A PROXY, WITH A PATTERN NOBODY TESTED. Visible-screen-only; --cursor 0 reading an EARLY slice; grepping ITEM EXIT unanchored and matching the brief's own instruction text; an incomplete spinner word list; testing a deploy with a root-layout class the item never touched; grep -E with a backslash-pipe, which is a LITERAL pipe, returning 0 hits for three DoD clauses on a spec carrying 47, 38 and 6 of them; git log --since silently matching nothing and nearly reporting three Stage 9 edits as never made; reading a work-done SUMMARY instead of the artefact; and grepping 'risk07' for 'RISK-07'. They err in BOTH directions — some invent a failure, some hide one.
learnings.why: Two of them would have destroyed or reverted shipped work: the root-layout class check said a live deploy had not landed, and the case-mismatched grep would have deleted eight worktrees whose work it could not see on master. The rules added are cheap: test the pattern before trusting its answer; when a check returns a surprising ABSENCE, verify the CHECK first; check the artefact never a summary; test something the item actually touched; and require TWO independent signals before acting destructively.

learnings.finding: THE CEO WAS THE CRITICAL PATH TWICE, BOTH SELF-INFLICTED, AND THEY ARE OPPOSITE ERRORS WITH ONE ROOT. DES-08 waited 10h 05m at a review gate the CEO ITSELF demanded, because the CEO stopped re-arming its watcher — found by the owner asking, not by any check. And the /brand merge was held about six hours as carve-out 3, outward-facing commitments, which NEVER APPLIED: the owner had commissioned a public brand page by name, with a reference URL, and commissioning a public page IS the outward-facing approval. Eleven of the sprint's remaining points sat behind a gate the CEO invented for itself.
learnings.why: Over-escalating and under-watching are the same failure: the CEO does not model itself as a resource that can be the bottleneck. Two standing checks now: before escalating, ask what the owner has ALREADY approved — a carve-out exists so you do not publish what they have not sanctioned, not to make you re-ask about the thing they specifically commissioned; and re-arm a watcher in the SAME tool call that reads its report, because a watcher's job ends the moment it fires.

learnings.finding: A GATE THAT HAS TO FIRE TWICE IS TELLING YOU THE DIAGNOSIS NEVER MOVED. SEO-04 parked in Sprint 02 because prices and capacities could not be sourced at scale. The CEO revived it by changing the METHOD — phone verification to published records — and it parked again on its bounded first pass. The second firing found the real cause, which neither park had named: nikahsatu.com is not a competitor we can out-build, it is the OPERATOR of the venues. Its footer reads 'copyright 2019 NikahSatu by Zest Venture Sdn Bhd', all four candidate brands route their own bookings through it, and the only published prices are its own undated discount packages. Decision 83 measured a venue operator publishing its own properties and called it a 17x directory advantage we should copy.
learnings.file_changed: skillcentral/agents/projects/hellokahwin/Marketing/head-of-seo-content.md — 'resolve the operator' moved from ethos PROSE to a PRE-FLIGHT checklist item, plus a new re-park question
learnings.why: Sprint 02's retro had already written 'resolve the operator before you rank a competitor' — in prose, in that same file's ethos section, where it did not fire. It is a pre-flight now because that is the only form that fires. And the CEO changed the method when the diagnosis was what was wrong, so any item handed back after a park now carries the question: what changed in the DIAGNOSIS, not the method?

learnings.finding: NO AUTOMATED CHECK IN THIS COMPANY COMPARES A COMPUTED COLOUR OR A CONTRAST RATIO. DES-08 found this against its own item. A CSS token collision producing invisible gold text would have shipped SITEWIDE with every automated check reporting green — structural-diff.py, the DES-09 checker and its own overflow script all compare structure, never a pixel or a CSS value. It was caught by eye, on one crop, at one breakpoint, only because the affected text happened to sit in the first fold of the first screenshot reviewed closely. DES-03's specification carries 47 MEASURED contrast ratios that nothing verifies.
learnings.why: This is the sprint's most valuable near-miss and the mechanism that caught it was a human looking, which is not a mechanism. On a redesign whose entire premise is 'stop looking generic', invisible text would have shipped through every gate. The agent volunteered this against the value of its own item rather than reporting a clean pass.

learnings.finding: FOUR AGENTS CORRECTED THE CEO WITH BETTER EVIDENCE THAN THE BRIEF THEY WERE GIVEN, and every correction arrived INSIDE a deliverable rather than as an argument. DES-06: the CEO briefed 'the site has no search at all' from decision 76; the agent measured and found search EXISTS and returns zero results for 84.3% of real arrival queries covering 70.9% of a month's impressions. SEO-10: the CEO called FAQ schema 'the cheapest rich-result opportunity we have'; the agent established Google RETIRED the FAQ rich result on 7 May 2026 and said so against its own item's value. SEO-08: decisions 88 and 97 both call /garden-wedding an 'English-intent page'; it is 2,332 words of Malay over twenty named Malaysian venues, and what is English is the QUERY, which killed the rewrite option the CEO had listed first. SEO-09: the DoD said 'all 13 articles'; the agent delivered 9 and declined 4 on the authority of CONT-04, the item's own named input, which the CEO had not read.
learnings.file_changed: docs/boardroom/decision-log.md (entries 144 and 89-97) — recorded, not corrected away
learnings.why: Third consecutive sprint in which the team disproved the CEO more often than the reverse. The pattern to protect: corrections that arrive as work, not as debate. The pattern to fix: the CEO writing DoDs from summaries instead of from the plans those summaries cite.

learnings.finding: THE STATUS BOARD'S DOCUMENTED TELL IS WRONG IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION. Sprint 02's retro says a stalled agent reads IDLE/DONE. On 28 Aug four agents stalled on 'Login expired' and the board showed all four as WORKING. Later the same day it correctly reported AUTH-STALL for the identical condition. So neither string is trustworthy alone: IDLE/DONE can mean finished OR frozen, and WORKING can mean working OR frozen.
learnings.why: Only reading the terminal distinguishes them, and an auth stall is a FLEET event — every occurrence in Sprint 03 hit two or more agents simultaneously, which is exactly why 'a sibling agent's watcher will wake me' fails as a strategy.

learnings.finding: run-stats.py PRODUCED A REAL CARD FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THREE SPRINTS, and its first output is the retro's most useful number: Sprint 03 ran 6h 56m ACTIVE against 25h 39m ELAPSED — 73% idle. Two gaps account for 60% of the span: DES-08 waiting 10h 05m, and a 5h 41m gap overlapping the /brand hold. Neither was an agent being slow.
learnings.file_changed: PLAT-12 shipped the fix (buddy 11e40e6); endsprint/SKILL.md already carried the --sprint correction
learnings.why: Carried forward twice and reported honestly as empty twice, which by this skill's own rule meant the template was wrong rather than the run. Now that effort is measurable, the sprint's real defect is visible as a number instead of an anecdote — and it is IDLE TIME, not throughput.

process_findings: WHAT HELD: the review gate held, and it held under pressure. DES-08 presented 'verification is complete with real evidence' and offered to ship; the CEO refused to take that on a summary and demanded the four named regression checks, each with both sides quoted. Three of the four guarded fixes that had shipped THAT SAME DAY — SEO-07's generateMetadata fix, SEO-10's FAQPage emitter, SEO-09's pillar up-links — and all four passed against live production, measured by the CEO rather than the agent. The ship check also earned its keep twice at the close: SEO-09 emitted ITEM EXIT: 0 with 13 files including a production UNDO.sql unmerged on a branch, and both design agents left their Stage 9 persona edits uncommitted. Both were caught by the sweep, not by the agents. WHAT BROKE: not verification this time, but ORCHESTRATION and ESCALATION. 73% of elapsed time was idle, and the two large gaps were both the CEO — once by not watching, once by not deciding. Three auth stalls cost about an hour between them, an order of magnitude less than the CEO's own two gaps. ORDERING WORKED: risk ran first, the design chain ran in dependency order (DES-01 rationale, DES-02 direction, DES-03 spec, DES-05 system, DES-08 implementation), and gates held their downstream items rather than being waved through. PARKING WORKED: SEO-04 is the only parked item and it is the most valuable 8 points in the sprint — a parked item with a clear reason cost 8 points; a directory of plausible invented capacities would have cost the thing the product sells, and would have been the hardest thing to detect months later. WHAT NEEDS FIXING NEXT: we can see WHEN work stopped and never WHY — the sprint's idle had to be reconstructed from completion timestamps plus one person's memory of the incidents, which a CEO reading this in three sprints could not do. That is PLAT-14.
shipped_check: EVERY ITEM IS VISIBLE TO THE OWNER. Verified at close across all three working trees — hellokahwin (docs), hellokahwin-site, and buddy — each with zero unpushed commits. Live and checkable: the redesigned homepage, catalogue and article at hellokahwin.com; the wordmark in the production header; /brand with five downloadable lockups; FAQPage JSON-LD on 29 articles; six formerly-noindexed hub URLs now index,follow and re-crawled by Google after the owner pressed Request Indexing; nine legacy articles re-parented with no URL moved; C2.1 complete at eight articles. In the repos: the design system at src/design-system/, the admin reference page, DES-03's 865KB specification, DES-09's runnable guardrail checker, and 17 work-done entries. Two artifacts: the three-direction canvas and the hardened specification. NOTHING was marked done without shipping — but SEO-09 tried to, and the ship check caught it.
carried_forward: PLAT-13 (backlog, 2pt) — watch-agent.sh wakes on every `curl` line via its ^HTTP/ milestone pattern, and every DoD on this team demands curl verification. SEO-09 and RISK-08 each tripped it 3+ times on ordinary work and never once on a completion. Do NOT simply delete the pattern: the self-test deliberately asserts HTTP/2 200 and HTTP/1.1 502 MUST fire, because in Sprint 02 a deploy returning those WAS the outcome. Make it context-aware, not absent.
